title: Paul starts his bread shop (paraphrase)
topic: A baker named Paul opens his new bakery on a Monday morning; the first customers arrive and the shelves are empty by evening
tail_E: The next morning he again pushes the first trays of dough into the hot
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'oven' is the natural completion of 'pushes the first trays of dough into the hot' in the bakery context; it does not occur in the units or the tail, nor does its German equivalent 'Ofen' / 'Backofen'. ' oven' is a single Pythia token (id 14195). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' oven') = 0.13 on the all-English rendering, rank 1.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase of family F06
notes: Formulation B: independent re-phrasing of the ten F06A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Paul). Replacements include bakery/bread shop (Bäckerei/Brotladen), on a Monday morning/early one Monday (an einem Montagmorgen/früh an einem Montag), kneads/makes (knetet/macht), lamps burn/lights shine (Lampen brennen/Lichter leuchten), a neighbor brings flowers to the door/Paul's neighbor brings a bouquet to the entrance (Nachbarin bringt Blumen an die Tür/Pauls Nachbarin bringt einen Strauß zum Eingang), the smell of bread fills the street/the street smells of bread (Duft erfüllt die Straße/Straße riecht nach Brot; subject changed to the street), customer buys/buyer takes (Kunde kauft/Käufer nimmt), coins behind the counter/money at the till (Münzen hinter der Theke/Geld an der Kasse), his wife writes/Paul's wife marks the prices (schreibt/notiert), customers fill/many customers crowd (Kunden füllen/viele Kunden bevölkern), first day ends/opening day closes (erster Tag endet/Eröffnungstag schließt). 'eröffnet' (unit 1) is inseparable; no separable verbs are used. Present tense and positive polarity throughout.
